text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Lower house of parliament voted in favour of creating a special bi-cameral commission to draft proposed constitutional reforms. Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema says he is ready to assume the chairmanship of the new commission (all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi met dairy farmers' representatives to halt protests over European Union milk quotas but no major breakthrough occurred. Milk producers have been blocking roads around Milan's airport since last Thursday.

* EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Italy has a problem of credibility over constant delays in plans to privatise state telecom group Stet and prepare for the liberalisation of the telecom sector. "Who is in charge here, Stet or the government?" he asked polemically (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party said "disagreement remains deep" with the goverment over the sell-off of Stet (all)
* Banks are expected to ease their lending rates after the Bank of Italy cut the discount rate by 75 basis points on Tuesday.
* Finance police investigating tax evasion discovered 36 trillion lire of "hidden revenues" in 1996 (all).

* Labour minister Tiziano Treu said a solution to the long-running dispute over metalworkers' contract renewal might be reached in a couple of days. Tomorrow PM Romano Prodi is due to meet trades union representatives (all).
* Information technology group Olivetti is expected to "clean up" its 1996 financial statements reviewing the value of loss-making units (Sole 24 Ore).

* US lawyer Edward Gottesman, who led a group of domestic and international investors to buy Olivetti's ailing PC division, is reportedly also interested in bike company Bianchi and porcelain producer Richard Ginori (Sole 24 Ore).
**Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
